paper.title: Restless-UCB, an Efficient and Low-complexity Algorithm for Online Restless Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Online restless bandit with birth-death Markov chains
unmapped: Each arm's state follows a Markov chain with M states that transitions every round regardless of pulls; player observes the state and reward of the pulled arm only
Regret is against the optimal (belief-state) policy with full knowledge of transitions and rewards, via the optimal average reward mu*
Rewards monotone non-increasing in state index (Assumption 1)
Neighbor transition probabilities lower bounded by c_1 (Assumption 4)
Access to an offline oracle returning the optimal (or approximate) policy
settings.definition_quote: Consider an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ which has one player (decision maker) and $N$ arms ... Each arm $i$ is associated with a Markov chain $M_i$. All the Markov chains have the same state space $S = \{1,2,\cdots,M\}$ ... this action gives a reward $x(t) \in [0,1]$ ... $Reg(T) = T\mu^*(\mathcal{R}) - \sum_{t=1}^T \E[x^\pi(t)]$.

symbols.M_st: number of states of each arm's Markov chain (paper's M)
symbols.d_min: minimum stationary probability over all arms and states
symbols.lambda_max: max over arms of the sup of second largest eigenvalue modulus over the neighbourhood of transition matrices

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: monotone rewards in state, birth-death chains, P_i(k,k+1)+P_i(k+1,k)<=1, neighbor transitions >= c_1
Oracle returns the exact optimal policy of the offline instance

source.label: Theorem_1
source.quote: If \texttt{Oracle} returns the optimal policy, then under Assumptions 1, 2, 3 and 4, the regret of Restless-UCB with $m(T) = T^{2\over 3}$ in an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ satisfies: $Reg(T) = \tilde{O}\left(\left({N\over d_{\min}} + {M^3\over (1-\lambda_{\max})^2}\right)T^{2\over 3}\right)$.

results.notes: Paper's N (number of arms) mapped to K. Regret defined as T*mu* minus expected cumulative reward, against optimal policy; classified as pseudo_regret. Polynomial complexity assumes an efficient oracle. Proof also hides constants such as a diameter constant C and dependence on c_1.

conditions: Oracle returns an approximate policy with ratio lambda

source.label: Proposition_Approx
source.quote: If \texttt{Oracle} returns an approximate policy with ratio $\lambda$, then under Assumptions 1, 2, 3 and 4, the approximation regret (with approximate ratio $\lambda$) of Restless-UCB with $m(T) = T^{2\over 3}$ in an online restless bandit problem $\mathcal{R}$ is upper bounded by $\tilde{O}(T^{2\over 3})$.

results.notes: Quantity is lambda-approximation regret (lambda*T*mu* - expected reward). Hidden constant may be exponential in N, M (depends on a diameter D).
